claims.statement: FilesystemMiddleware proactively evicts tool-result text only when it exceeds its configured character-derived threshold; it writes the full text to a sanitized tool-call path, returns a recoverable pointer-and-preview replacement only after a successful backend write, and otherwise keeps the original message.

Large tool-result previews are line-numbered head-and-tail views that explicitly distinguish omitted middle lines from individually clipped long lines, and the replacement preserves ToolMessage identity and non-text content blocks.

FilesystemMiddleware configures large-result and conversation-history paths beneath CompositeBackend.artifacts_root when available, otherwise under root-level paths, so recovery requires read_file to resolve the backend path that received the write.

Oversized human messages retain their full checkpointed content while being tagged with lc_evicted_to and replaced by a preview only in model requests; the same-id state update avoids clobbering an AI response in the same graph step, and write failure leaves the message untagged and untruncated.

SummarizationMiddleware retains raw messages and reconstructs the model-visible conversation from a summary event followed by the retained suffix; the event records its cutoff, summary message, and optional archive path.

When compaction is selected, SummarizationMiddleware archives older non-summary messages in a timestamped per-session markdown history, reuses a persisted internally generated session id, and can continue with an in-context summary when archive writing fails.

Before archival and summary generation, inline data media is uploaded once per content hash under conversation_history/media and rewritten to path references; decode or upload failures are represented by failed-offload placeholders rather than silently omitted.

Summarization considers the complete request, including system prompt and optionally tool schemas, and compacts when either its configured trigger fires or the request exceeds the calculated input budget.

The overflow fallback recognizes context-limit failures but not unrelated bad requests, clips only a trailing consecutive ToolMessage batch, preserves read_file recoverability by pointing to its original source path, and persists generic results through large-result eviction.

Context-overflow recovery sends at most one strictly smaller retry, rejects known over-budget reduced requests before calling the provider, and raises a terminal ContextOverflowError after recovery is exhausted.

End-to-end tests verify that overflow clipping uses the original file path without duplicate artifacts for read_file results, while ls and arbitrary tool results are stored under large_tool_results by tool-call id.

CompositeBackend defaults artifacts_root to "/", routes paths by longest matching prefix, and its synchronous and asynchronous read/write methods preserve the public full path while delegating the stripped path to the selected backend; an artifact root can therefore place middleware artifacts on a routed backend.

The sync and async context-management paths have matching offload and recovery semantics: they use write/awrite counterparts, retain original messages on failed generic offload, and enforce the same bounded overflow retry, while asynchronous history archiving and summary creation run concurrently after media processing.

Artifact-root tests verify that custom roots are normalized and used for synchronous and asynchronous tool-result eviction, conversation-history placement, and large human-message offload rather than falling back to root-level artifact directories.

UnsupportedContentMiddleware replaces explicitly unsupported image, audio, video, and file blocks only in HumanMessage and ToolMessage model requests; it preserves the original graph-state content so a later capable model can receive it, and its read_file placeholder identifies the source path.

SummarizationToolMiddleware exposes an eligibility-gated compact_conversation tool for explicit compaction, reuses a configured SummarizationMiddleware, and updates the same summary-event and session-id state used by automatic compaction.

MemoryMiddleware loads configured sources into private state once, skips missing files but raises on other download errors, and injects ordered, comment-stripped memory into the model system prompt without changing the underlying user messages.

Deep-agent graph assembly appends provider-specific prompt caching before MemoryMiddleware, and MemoryMiddleware can place an Anthropic-only ephemeral cache-control marker on the final system block so the memory boundary is cacheable independently of the static prompt.

Dcode's RemoteAgent offload client keeps one operation id across hook-resume rounds, validates terminal results, limits hook fulfillments to 32, and on caller cancellation waits for the server's operation-specific cancelled-or-finished acknowledgement before re-raising cancellation.

The server-owned offload boundary serializes a thread operation, refuses active or pending work, reads and rechecks the checkpoint before commit, and permits only summary/session/cost state channels so it cannot overwrite conversation messages.

Dcode reserves the checkpoint summary before appending an offload archive, then links the archive path; an archive append is guarded against prerequisite read failures, confirmed link failure rolls the append back, and an unconfirmable link is surfaced as indeterminate.

Local dcode conversation-history storage prefers a hardened per-user directory, marks fallback temporary storage as ephemeral, and performs best-effort retention and thread-deletion cleanup without allowing cleanup failures or suspicious thread ids to delete arbitrary paths.

Remote state recovery retries one conflicted state update only after concurrently cancelling pending and running server runs with bounded waits; abandonment closes only trailing unanswered tool calls before clearing pending graph work.
